# ISSUE-601 implementation plan

Make the generated config and assisted onboarding teach the same role settings, then show maintainers which settings doctor and task preflight actually use. The approved sensitive profile applies. Estimate 4–7 hours for implementation and focused verification, with time for independent review and coordinator validation within the 16-hour claim budget.

## What we know

- The shipped scaffold selects Codex and native isolated execution, and currently omits the role map. Init uses the managed writer for preservation and upgrading. See `internal/harness/templates/swarm/config.yaml:8` and `internal/harness/scaffold.go:277`.
- Onboarding is a printed guide available before init. The CLI and generated slash commands share the embedded guide, and both checked-in copies matched it byte-for-byte. See `internal/cli/onboard.go:10`, `internal/harness/onboard.go:14`, and `internal/harness/scaffold.go:505`.
- Work preflight loads config, workflow and checks from `state.BaseSHA`. Its role selection considers phase, artifacts, approval, continuation and interactive planning. Doctor independently selects checkout defaults. See `internal/workflow/engine.go:404`, `:459`, `:565`, `:2106`, `:2113` and `internal/cli/doctor.go:60`, `:186`.
- Linux `execution.mode: isolated` with `backend: native` uses the native Codex boundary for Codex and the Bubblewrap tool executor for Claude Code and OpenCode 2. The latter requires OpenCode 2.1.2 or later. Existing inspection selects and probes these paths. See `internal/agent/configured.go:81`, `:140`, `:177` and `docs/harness/opencode.md:7`. Config parsing validates effort, and agent preflight validates role admission. See `internal/harness/scaffold.go:644`, `internal/contract/effort.go:25`, and `internal/agent/configured.go:257`.
- The text dry-run currently prints capabilities and blockers. JSON already exposes policy and the selected agent and binary maps. See `internal/cli/work.go:168` and `internal/workflow/engine.go:164`.

## What we're assuming

- Use commented examples under an active empty role map or a commented role map with four visible keys. Verify the emitted YAML decodes with no explicit role assignments and that switching just `default_agent` changes all four inherited selections.
- Use `opencode-go/glm-5` as a sample OpenCode Go model identifier. Verify the exact provider/model string round-trips through the guide, parser and preview. Model availability remains a harness/provider setting.
- The supplied approved snapshot hides Git metadata. `changes/unreleased/601.md` is absent from the snapshot, including as a symlink. Recheck at the recorded base where Git metadata is available before adding it. This is the sole new production file.

## Open questions

- Offline fixtures can verify routing, diagnostics and the configured model identifier without provider access. Live model availability and installed-runtime readiness depend on the operator environment. Use the documented harness prerequisites and existing probes, and keep live provider execution outside acceptance verification.

## Implementation

1. Update `internal/harness/templates/swarm/config.yaml` near `default_agent` with planner, reviewer, developer and tester examples. Explain inheritance, named entries, explicit `harness` for custom aliases, and optional model and effort. Keep the actual default values and existing named entries. Verify current managed-file behavior with a customized config and normal init without force.
2. Extend `internal/harness/templates/commands/swarm-onboard.md` and mirror it to `.claude/commands/swarm-onboard.md` and `.opencode/commands/swarm-onboard.md`. Have the guide inspect and preserve the existing config before init, propose a diff scoped to the intended role/agent entries, request agreement before applying, and run `swarm repo doctor` after applying. Ship one fenced YAML example intended to merge into the existing config. Map planner and tester to distinct Codex aliases with `gpt-6.2-sol`, medium and high effort respectively, reviewer to a Claude Code alias with a model and reviewer allowlist, and developer to an OpenCode alias with the Go model and omitted effort. All aliases declare their harness and binary. Preserve existing default, unrelated policy, entries and comments, and call out reviewer eligibility and existing allowlists when proposing the edit. Explain the unattended planner mode, the agent gate's reviewer, independent human approval for human gates, and deterministic required checks. Show how to review and commit the change, land it on the task's target branch, then have an authorized maintainer re-approve affected existing WorkUnits with `swarm issue approve <issue>` after resolving any active claim, respecting existing plan re-review rules. Adjust help in `internal/cli/onboard.go` to describe the guided role edit while keeping prompt and JSON behavior.
3. In `internal/workflow/engine.go`, factor the existing selector so it can return entry and winning source together. Keep `ResolveRoleAgent`'s string interface and exact precedence. Build an ordered, presentation-only role preview containing role, disposition and reason, plus entry, source, harness, configured model and effort where selected. Reuse existing agent harness resolution through a small pure metadata function in `internal/agent/configured.go` using the same lookup conventions as the runner. Represent unset fields as harness defaults in text, deriving metadata even when inspection reports a blocker. Preserve invalid selections as diagnostics.
4. Build task rows inside inspect-only preflight from the same phase, approval and continuation decisions used to populate the execution maps. Identify the interactive planner as manual, and when its existing shortcut stops selection, mark later roles as deferred until plans are staged. Show an applicable human gate as manual while pending and show phase exclusions, existing plan/approval, and continuation skips as applicable. Keep these rows advisory and leave role admission, gate resolution, inspection, execution maps and control flow intact. In `internal/cli/work.go`, add the rows to text and expose them additively within the existing JSON payload, with approved task policy and base identity. Keep continuation, capabilities and blockers.
5. In `internal/cli/doctor.go` use the same selector without CLI overrides. Enrich each existing selected execution check with checkout policy, selection source, harness, model and effort, retaining optional harness checks, probe outcomes and status. Surface selected reviewer eligibility with the existing task-policy diagnostic or its shared predicate, alongside existing role admission and strict config checks. Doctor describes configured defaults even if a particular task would skip a role. Keep the existing output envelope and add only information needed for the role preview.
6. Add `changes/unreleased/601.md` with one user-facing bullet. Complete the focused checks below. Estimate under five minutes per focused command with prepared caches.

## HANDOFF

- Edit the config template at line 8, the embedded onboard guide at steps 4–7 and its two command copies, and `internal/cli/onboard.go:10`. Extend `internal/harness/scaffold_test.go:239`, `:803`, and `internal/cli/cli_test.go:1822`.
- Extend `PreflightResult`, `ResolveRoleAgent` and `preflight` in `internal/workflow/engine.go:164`, `:285`, `:336`; use `internal/agent/configured.go:33`, `:322` for display metadata. Extend the renderers in `internal/cli/work.go:168` and `internal/cli/doctor.go:186`. Use the doctor and execution fixtures in `internal/cli/doctor_test.go:22` and `internal/cli/execution_test.go:23`, plus the reviewer policy fixture in `internal/workflow/reviewer_policy_test.go:16`.
- Focused commands:

  ```bash
  go test ./internal/harness -run '^Test(ConfigRejectsInvalidSecurityPolicy|DecodeConfigAgentEffort|InitPreservesExistingPolicyAndRejectsMutablePins|InitDryRunReportsWithoutWriting|OnboardingGuideIsAPlainPrompt|RoleDefaultsScaffold|OnboardingRoleExample)$' -count=1
  go test ./internal/cli -run '^Test(RepoOnboardAndInitDryRun|Doctor.*|WorkRolePreview.*|DryRunReportsIsolationBlockersWithoutClaim|ToolCapabilityOptionalFailureDryRun|Issue466WorkDryRunResume|WorkProgressCanBeDisabledAndDryRunIsSilent)$' -count=1
  go test ./internal/workflow -run '^Test(ResolveRoleAgentSelection|PreflightRejectsReviewerOutsideReviewerAgents|ToolCapabilityInjectedBoundaryPreflight)$' -count=1
  go vet ./internal/agent ./internal/workflow ./internal/cli ./internal/harness
  ```
- Checked the rollout assumptions against the managed init entry point, actual flags in `internal/cli/work.go:278`, re-approval command in `internal/cli/issue.go:112`, documented claim and re-review behavior in `docs/developer.md:524`, and the two matching onboarding command copies.
- Reopen the plan if correct reporting requires changing role execution, approved-base selection, phase/gate semantics, isolation, or adapter capabilities. Reopen if the supplied mixed example needs a new adapter or config field.
- **What this change breaks**. The checked-in slash-command copies need the same guide edits as the embedded template. Keep the onboarding guide's existing CLI intro and flags compatible with `TestRepoOnboardAndInitDryRun`. Preserve the selected/optional distinction and capability rendering checked in `internal/cli/doctor_test.go`, and preserve the continuation and quiet progress behavior checked in `internal/cli/issue324_retry_test.go:539` and `internal/cli/work_progress_test.go:65`. Existing PR and coordinator callers of `ResolveRoleAgent`, preflight agent/binary maps and capability reports keep their current interfaces. README, the admin guide and workflow docs describe the same prompt-only onboarding entry point and remain accurate.

# ISSUE-601 test plan

Run local Git fixtures and in-process or stubbed inspection paths. The execution paths under test are Linux isolated native Codex and Linux native backend with Bubblewrap-owned tools for Claude Code and OpenCode 2. Doctor inspects checkout settings. Task dry-run inspects approved task settings. The fixtures cover policy selection, required admission checks and rendering without provider requests.

## Acceptance coverage

| Criterion | Cases and evidence |
| --- | --- |
| 1. Fresh scaffold, inheritance and preservation | `TestRoleDefaultsScaffold` uses real init and checks each visible role key and the guidance for inheritance and named entries. Load the emitted config and assert Codex is the inherited entry for all roles, model and effort are unset, and the isolated native defaults persist. Change only `default_agent` in fixture YAML and verify all four roles inherit it. Extend `TestInitPreservesExistingPolicyAndRejectsMutablePins` with customized role/agent settings and unrelated YAML, then confirm byte-identical contents after regular init. |
| 2. Assisted onboarding | Extend `TestRepoOnboardAndInitDryRun` to cover text and JSON, with no file writes and a guide that asks for a diff and agreement before applying. In `TestOnboardingRoleExample`, extract the actual fenced example from the embedded guide and merge its role and agent entries into a generated config with unrelated customized defaults. Load it through existing strict checks and assert all four aliases, harnesses, model IDs, distinct Codex efforts and reviewer admission. Assert unrelated defaults remain intact. Check the two shipped command copies match the embedded guide and independently read the guide for the edit, review, commit, approval and required-check sequence. |
| 3. Doctor and task dry-run display | Extend doctor fixtures for selected and optional roles, inherited and explicit sources, configured values, harness defaults, and checkout policy labeling. In `TestWorkRolePreviewApprovedBase`, approve a local issue on the mixed config, then commit different checkout role settings. Compare doctor against text and JSON dry-run. Task rows must follow the pinned base and show role, entry, harness, model, effort and source. Test agent gate selection and a human gate with interactive planning using `TestWorkRolePreviewManualAndSkipped`. Assert no reviewer is probed for human review and roles deferred by interactive planning are identified. Add an already-staged or continuation case and a phase-specific case to check omitted roles. Check no claim or new task worktree appears. |
| 4. Offline regressions, precedence and diagnostics | In `TestResolveRoleAgentSelection`, table-test each role through role CLI override, generic CLI override, explicit role config and inherited default, including winning source. In `TestWorkRolePreviewApprovedBase` exercise real CLI flags together. Reuse the mixed guide example's values for the preview fixture. Extend `TestDoctorRejectsExcludedSelectedRole`, keep `TestPreflightRejectsReviewerOutsideReviewerAgents`, and add a selected-but-disallowed entry to dry-run in `TestWorkRolePreviewDiagnostics`. Assert a role and entry-specific error with policy context and a path to choose an allowed entry. Use `TestDecodeConfigAgentEffort` and a CLI invalid-config fixture to check an OpenCode effort reports supported harnesses and an invalid Codex effort reports accepted values. Ensure invalid policy prevents normal execution. Use missing or controlled fixture binaries and existing inspection seams. Unexpected runner or provider entry points should fail the tests. |

## Developer checks

Run the focused commands from the candidate checkout and record command, result, candidate commit or diff identity, and fixture/runtime limitations in the implementation artifact.

```bash
go test ./internal/harness -run '^Test(ConfigRejectsInvalidSecurityPolicy|DecodeConfigAgentEffort|InitPreservesExistingPolicyAndRejectsMutablePins|InitDryRunReportsWithoutWriting|OnboardingGuideIsAPlainPrompt|RoleDefaultsScaffold|OnboardingRoleExample)$' -count=1
go test ./internal/cli -run '^Test(RepoOnboardAndInitDryRun|Doctor.*|WorkRolePreview.*|DryRunReportsIsolationBlockersWithoutClaim|ToolCapabilityOptionalFailureDryRun|Issue466WorkDryRunResume|WorkProgressCanBeDisabledAndDryRunIsSilent)$' -count=1
go test ./internal/workflow -run '^Test(ResolveRoleAgentSelection|PreflightRejectsReviewerOutsideReviewerAgents|ToolCapabilityInjectedBoundaryPreflight)$' -count=1
go vet ./internal/agent ./internal/workflow ./internal/cli ./internal/harness
gofmt -l internal/agent/configured.go internal/cli/{onboard,doctor,work,cli_test,doctor_test,execution_test}.go internal/harness/scaffold_test.go internal/workflow/engine.go
cmp internal/harness/templates/commands/swarm-onboard.md .claude/commands/swarm-onboard.md
cmp internal/harness/templates/commands/swarm-onboard.md .opencode/commands/swarm-onboard.md
git diff --check
```

Include any additional modified Go test files in the format check. Verify that the test filter actually selects the new cases. Focused checks are expected to take less than five minutes each with prepared caches.

## Independent tester review

Read the candidate diff and inspect fixtures against all four rows of the acceptance matrix. Independently trace checkout and approved-base loaders, the shared selector, interactive and human gate branches, role admission, and isolation checks. Confirm the preview consumes those decisions and that no preview data or override changes approved policy, executes model requests, or writes coordination state. Verify help and command examples against Cobra registrations. Inspect the re-approval guidance against the approved-base behavior and check the protected file diff is confined to the two authorized command copies. Evaluate the adversarial cases independently, including checkout policy divergence, a blocked selected role, and invalid effort. Record evidence and findings by criterion in the validation artifact, referencing applicable developer results by candidate identity. Repeat only when relevant source changes, a failure needs reproduction, or a coverage concern remains.

## Coordinator reference policy

The coordinator runs the complete trusted-base required validation policy once on the final candidate after the roles finish. The full required policy run is owned by the coordinator. Allow approximately 45–120 minutes depending on cache state and scheduling of the CI-tier CLI shards, whose configured budgets are up to 20 minutes each. Record check outputs in the coordinator's validation evidence tied to the final candidate, approved base, and policy digest. Submission and CI consumers use applicable authoritative results under existing policy. Agent observations remain advisory and cannot satisfy claim-bound validation or publication.

# Implementation Summary (Issue #601)

## What we learned

- Agent inspection wraps runtime errors for safe display. Use the capability report's role-denied reason to explain a policy denial without exposing the underlying runtime error.

## Developer report

# ISSUE-601 implementation

The generated config shows all four roles and how to inherit the default Codex entry. Assisted onboarding previews role and agent edits, includes a mixed-harness example, and explains validation and WorkUnit re-approval.

Doctor reports checkout role selections and reviewer eligibility. Issue work dry-run reports approved task selections and the approved base SHA in text and JSON. The preview derives its dispositions from the phase, gate, plan artifacts and continuation decisions. The existing runner selection and isolation checks still govern execution.

The first CLI run failed because the inspection wrapper hid the role denial behind a generic runtime message. The wrapper now reports role and entry when the capability report confirms policy denial. Runtime errors continue to use the sanitized diagnostic. The focused commands were rerun after this fix and the scaffold and fixture refinements. Both command-copy comparisons still apply because the guide and copies did not change after those checks. There were no prior role test results to reuse.

## HANDOFF

In particular, the CLI tests approve a mixed configuration on one commit, change the checkout configuration, and verify both policy sources. They also cover CLI precedence, interactive planning, human review, phase exclusions, continuation, role denial and invalid effort. Fixtures use local Git, unavailable harness paths and controlled mock execution. Live provider availability and installed-runtime readiness remain environment-dependent.
